newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's first lady brings Xmas turkeys for hostages.
newsitem.headline: Peru's first lady brings Xmas turkeys for hostages.

text.p: Peru's first lady Keiko Sofia Fujimori brought fancy turkey lunches on Wednesday for the 105 hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's home as a Christmas goodwill gesture.

Fujimori, the daughter of President Alberto Fujimori, crossed police lines and was driven to within 150 feet (50 metres) of the residence as a bus containing about 20 Government Palace chefs, each carrying a tray with a roast turkey decorated with fruit, waited nearby.

The 21-year-old first lady waited inside her bullet-proofed black S-Class Mercedes limousine for about five minutes near the residence before turning around and driving to a house about a block and a half from the scene which she entered accompanied by several plainclothes bodyguards.

Fujimori's arrival caused pandemonium among the hundreds of journalists following the hostage drama. One local photographer, Alex Ramon of the La Republica newspaper, was hit by the first lady's car as it approached the residence. Ramon was taken to a nearby hospital, apparently with a broken leg, a paramedic said.
The chefs, dressed in white peaked hats, white jackets and blue jeans unloaded the turkeys onto carts.
Red Cross helpers then pushed the trolleys down the street, through the main gate and delivered them to the grand front portal of the embassy residence.
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas were holding 105 hostages including Pedro Fujimori, the president's brother, inside.
Keiko Sofia has acted as first lady since President Fujimori divorced his wife, Susana, in 1995.
